intro: Every king had five names. Two of them are written in cartouches: the throne name, taken at the coronation, and the birth name. The throne name follows “King of Upper and Lower Egypt” (sedge and bee); the birth name follows “Son of Re” (duck and sun disk). Inside, a god’s name is written first out of respect. The printed cartouches below follow standard spellings; on the walls the same names are often arranged differently.

kings.name: Senusret I
kings.role: Built the White Chapel, a small limestone shrine decorated for his jubilee, now rebuilt in the Open Air Museum. It is one of the oldest buildings you can see at Karnak.

throne.name: Kheperkare
throne.meaning: The ka of Re comes into being
throne.look: Sun disk, scarab beetle and the raised arms of the ka.

birth.name: Senusret
birth.meaning: Man of the goddess Wosret
birth.look: Starts with the canine head on a staff (user), the sign also used in Usermaatre.

kings.spot: His cartouches cover the pillars of the White Chapel. Nectanebo I later used the same throne name, Kheperkare.

kings.name: Amenhotep I
kings.role: Built a calcite (Egyptian alabaster) chapel for Amun’s sacred bark, now reconstructed.

throne.name: Djeserkare
throne.meaning: Holy is the ka of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, an arm holding a wand (djeser, “holy”) and the ka arms.

birth.name: Amenhotep
birth.meaning: Amun is satisfied
birth.look: The Amun group with the offering table (hetep).

kings.spot: On the reconstructed calcite chapel.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Thutmose I
kings.role: Built the Fourth Pylon and an enclosure wall around the early temple of the 18th Dynasty.

throne.name: Aakheperkare
throne.meaning: Great is the form of the ka of Re
throne.look: Sun disk over a column (aa, “great”), scarab and ka arms.

birth.name: Thutmose
birth.meaning: Born of Thoth
birth.look: The ibis of Thoth followed by the three fox skins (mes, “born”).

kings.spot: Around the Fourth Pylon.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Hatshepsut
kings.role: A woman who ruled as king. She raised granite obelisks for her jubilee and built the Red Chapel, a resting place for Amun’s bark. The chapel was later taken apart; its blocks have been rebuilt in the Open Air Museum.

throne.name: Maatkare
throne.meaning: Maat is the ka of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, seated Maat and the ka arms.

birth.name: Khnemet-Amun Hatshepsut
birth.meaning: Joined with Amun, foremost of noble women
birth.look: The Amun group, a jug, the front of a lion (hat, “foremost”) and a seated noble.

kings.spot: On her standing obelisk and on the Red Chapel blocks in the Open Air Museum. Her names often end in the feminine t.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Thutmose III
kings.role: Built the Akhmenu festival hall in the east of the temple and reworked the sanctuary. His throne name Menkheperre is one of the most common at Karnak.

throne.name: Menkheperre
throne.meaning: Enduring are the forms of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, game board and scarab: short and easy to spot.

birth.name: Thutmose-neferkheperu
birth.meaning: Born of Thoth, beautiful of forms
birth.look: The ibis of Thoth, fox skins, heart-and-windpipe (nefer) and scarab.

kings.spot: All over the Akhmenu and the central part of the temple.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Thutmose IV
kings.role: Built a painted pillared court for a jubilee setting. It was later dismantled; its pillars have been rebuilt in the Open Air Museum.

throne.name: Menkheperure
throne.meaning: Enduring are the manifestations of Re
throne.look: Like Thutmose III’s name, plus three plural strokes.

birth.name: Thutmose
birth.meaning: Born of Thoth
birth.look: The ibis of Thoth and the fox skins.

kings.spot: On the painted pillars in the Open Air Museum. Count the strokes to tell him from Thutmose III.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Amenhotep III
kings.role: Built the Third Pylon, the eastern end of the Hypostyle Hall, filling its core with blocks from older monuments.

throne.name: Nebmaatre
throne.meaning: The lord of Maat is Re
throne.look: Sun disk, Maat and the basket (neb). Ramesses VI’s name begins with the same three signs.

birth.name: Amenhotep-heqawaset
birth.meaning: Amun is satisfied, ruler of Thebes
birth.look: The Amun group, offering table, crook (ruler) and the sceptre of Thebes.

kings.spot: On the Third Pylon at the east end of the Hall.

citations.locator: Third Pylon built by Amenhotep III
Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Akhenaten
kings.role: Began his reign as Amenhotep IV and built temples to the sun disk, the Aten, east of Karnak. They were pulled down after his death, and thousands of their small blocks (talatat) were reused, including in the foundations of the Hypostyle Hall.

throne.name: Neferkheperure-waenre
throne.meaning: Beautiful are the forms of Re, the unique one of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, nefer, scarab with plural strokes, a second sun disk.

birth.name: Akhenaten
birth.meaning: Effective for the Aten
birth.look: The Aten’s name (reed leaf, bread, water, sun disk) and the crested ibis (akh).

kings.spot: On talatat blocks from his temples; his names were often hacked out.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Horemheb
kings.dynasty: New Kingdom, last king of the 18th Dynasty
kings.role: Built the Second Pylon, the gateway you walk through into the Hall.

throne.name: Djeserkheperure-setepenre
throne.meaning: Holy are the manifestations of Re, chosen of Re
throne.look: An arm with a wand (djeser), scarab with plural strokes, adze and water.

birth.name: Horemheb-meryamun
birth.meaning: Horus is in festival, beloved of Amun
birth.look: The Amun group and hoe, the falcon of Horus and the festival bowl.

kings.spot: On the Second Pylon gateway at the west end of the Hall.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Ramesses I
kings.dynasty: New Kingdom, founder of the 19th Dynasty
kings.role: Father of Sety I. He reigned for about two years. Sety honoured him in scenes on the west wall of the Hall, and his names appear in their texts.

throne.name: Menpehtyre
throne.meaning: Enduring is the strength of Re
throne.look: Sun disk and game board with leopard heads (pehty, “strength”).

birth.name: Ramessu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him
birth.look: Sun disk, three fox skins, folded cloth: the basic Ramesses spelling.

kings.spot: In scenes where Sety I honours his late father on the west wall.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Sety I
kings.role: Builder of the Hall. All his carving inside it is in raised relief, mostly in the north half. He died before the decoration was finished.

throne.name: Menmaatre
throne.meaning: Enduring is the Maat of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, seated Maat, game board: short and compact.

birth.name: Sety-merenptah
birth.meaning: He of Seth, beloved of Ptah
birth.look: Includes a small seated figure of the god Seth.

kings.spot: His Menmaatre is the easiest royal name in the Hall to recognise. Try it at stop 6, marker 6.

citations.locator: Plate 48, p. 98; names of Sety I

photos.label: Birth name, painted on a roof fragment, with the seated Seth figure

kings.name: Ramesses II
kings.role: Sety’s son. He finished the Hall, converted the south half to sunk relief, and put his names on the central columns and almost everywhere else, sometimes over his father’s.

throne.name: Usermaatre-setepenre
throne.meaning: Strong is the Maat of Re, chosen of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, canine head (user), Maat, then adze and water with a second sun disk.

birth.name: Ramesses-meryamun
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, beloved of Amun
birth.look: The Amun group, sun disk, fox skins and folded cloth.

kings.spot: User + Maat + adze = Ramesses II. You will see it on the twelve central columns and on most of the south wall.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.early: In his first year his names were shorter: Usermaatre alone, and Ramessu-meryamun. He settled on the final forms in his second year and had earlier cartouches in the south half recut.

photos.label: Birth name painted on the Hall ceiling

kings.name: Sety II
kings.role: Built a triple bark shrine for Amun, Mut and Khonsu in what is now the Great Court.

throne.name: Userkheperure-setepenre
throne.meaning: Powerful are the manifestations of Re, chosen of Re
throne.look: User, scarab with plural strokes, adze.

birth.name: Sety-merenptah
birth.meaning: He of Seth, beloved of Ptah
birth.look: Like Sety I’s birth name, with the seated Seth figure.

kings.spot: On his bark shrine in the Great Court.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Ramesses III
kings.role: Built a bark temple in the Great Court and began the Temple of Khonsu. In the Hall he added inscriptions and a small shrine for visitors against the outside of the north wall.

throne.name: Usermaatre-meryamun
throne.meaning: Strong is the Maat of Re, beloved of Amun
throne.look: Starts like Ramesses II’s name, but ends with the Amun group and hoe instead of the adze.

birth.name: Ramesses-heqaiunu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, ruler of Heliopolis
birth.look: A seated sun god, fox skins and the crook (ruler).

kings.spot: If you see Usermaatre without the adze, check whether it is Ramesses III.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Ramesses IV
kings.role: Filled most of the 134 columns with friezes of his cartouches and extra scenes. His names appear thousands of times. He also carved huge cartouches and Horus names at the bases of the central columns.

throne.name: Heqamaatre-setepenamun
throne.meaning: Re is the ruler of Maat, chosen of Amun
throne.look: Sun disk, crook (heqa), feather of Maat, adze and the Amun group. Early in his reign: Usermaatre-setepenamun.

birth.name: Ramesses-heqamaat-meryamun
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, ruler of Maat, beloved of Amun
birth.look: Figures of Amun and Re, fox skins, the crook and Maat.

kings.spot: Rows of identical small cartouches on the column shafts are usually his. He changed the spelling of his name and recut some of them.

citations.locator: Large cartouches at the base of the great columns
Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Ramesses VI
kings.role: Took over some of Ramesses IV’s big cartouches at the bases of the central columns by carving his own names over them. Plaster hid the earlier names; where it has fallen, several names overlap.

throne.name: Nebmaatre-meryamun
throne.meaning: The lord of Maat is Re, beloved of Amun
throne.look: Sun disk, a figure of Amun, Maat, hoe and basket.

birth.name: Ramesses-Amunherkhepeshef-netjerheqaiunu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, Amun is his strength, god and ruler of Heliopolis
birth.look: Sun disk, Amun figure, fox skins, god flag, crook and the column of Heliopolis.

kings.spot: At the bases of the central columns, a cartouche with a confusing jumble of signs may hold two or three kings’ names at once.

citations.locator: Ramesses VI usurped Ramesses IV’s cartouches

kings.name: Herihor
kings.role: High Priest of Amun at Karnak who took royal titles in the temple. He added bands of text low down on walls and columns, linking himself with Sety I and Ramesses II.

throne.name: First Priest of Amun
throne.meaning: His priestly title, written inside a cartouche
throne.look: A cartouche that holds a priest’s title: the god flag, a club and a head (“first”), and the Amun group.

birth.name: Siamun-Herihor
birth.meaning: Son of Amun, Horus is raised up
birth.look: The Amun group, the sky sign and the falcon of Horus.

kings.spot: Low bands of text at the bottom of the walls; many are worn or lost.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Shoshenq I
kings.role: A king of Libyan descent whose reliefs by the Bubastite Portal, in the Great Court, proclaim victories in Syria-Palestine.

throne.name: Hedjkheperre-setepenre
throne.meaning: Bright are the forms of Re, chosen of Re
throne.look: The white crown (hedj, “bright”), scarab and adze.

birth.name: Shoshenq-meryamun
birth.meaning: Shoshenq, beloved of Amun
birth.look: The Amun group and hoe, then lotus pools and a hill (the sounds sh-sh-n-q).

kings.spot: Beside the Bubastite Portal. His name ring is followed by rows of captives holding foreign place names.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

photos.label: Small cartouches at the top of the relief

kings.name: Taharqo
kings.role: A king from Kush (in today’s Sudan). He built a huge kiosk with ten columns in the Great Court; one column still stands.

throne.name: Nefertemkhure
throne.meaning: Nefertem is his protector
throne.look: Sun disk, heart-and-windpipe (nefer) and a sledge (tem).

birth.name: Taharqo
birth.meaning: Taharqo (his Kushite name)
birth.look: Land sign, twisted wick (h), lion (rw) and hill (q): a foreign name spelled by sound.

kings.spot: In the Great Court around his standing column.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Hakoris
kings.role: Built a small bark station near the temple entrance, where Amun’s bark could rest.

throne.name: Khnemmaatre
throne.meaning: Who embraces the Maat of Re
throne.look: Sun disk, a jug (khnem, “unite”) and Maat.

birth.name: Hakor
birth.meaning: Hakor
birth.look: Spelled by sound: twisted wick (h), basket (k), mouth (r).

kings.spot: On his bark station at the entrance to the temple.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Nectanebo I
kings.role: One of the last native kings of Egypt. The unfinished First Pylon and the great mudbrick enclosure walls are linked with his building work.

throne.name: Kheperkare
throne.meaning: The ka of Re comes into being
throne.look: Sun disk, scarab and ka arms: the same throne name as Senusret I, 1,600 years earlier.

birth.name: Nakhtnebef
birth.meaning: Strong one of his lord
birth.look: A tree and sieve sign (nakht), an arm with a stick, and the basket (neb).

kings.spot: Around the entrance and the enclosure.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Philip III Arrhidaeus
kings.role: Half-brother of Alexander the Great. Egyptian craftsmen rebuilt the granite bark shrine at the heart of the temple in his name.

throne.name: Setepenre-meryamun
throne.meaning: Chosen of Re, beloved of Amun
throne.look: A Greek king given an Egyptian throne name.

birth.name: Philip
birth.meaning: Philippos, written in hieroglyphs
birth.look: Stool (p), recumbent lion for l, stool again (p), reed leaves (i) and s: a Greek name spelled by sound.

kings.spot: In the granite bark shrine at the centre of the temple. Look for the lion used for the sound l, a late invention for Greek names.

citations.locator: Infobox royal names, hieroglyph spelling and reign

kings.name: Ptolemy VIII
kings.role: Decorated the Temple of Opet, with its raised sanctuary and crypts linked to Osiris.

throne.name: Iwaennetjerwyperwy-setepenptah-irymaatre-sekhemankhenamun
throne.meaning: Heir of the two gods who appear, chosen of Ptah, who does the Maat of Re, living image of Amun
throne.look: A very long Ptolemaic throne name: look for Ptah’s name (stool, bread, twisted wick) and the adze.

birth.name: Ptolemy-ankhdjet-meryptah
birth.meaning: Ptolemy, living forever, beloved of Ptah
birth.look: Stool (p), bread (t), lasso (wa), lion (l), owl (m): Ptolemaios spelled by sound.

kings.spot: In the Temple of Opet. Late names like this are long and full of extra signs.
